memory_update.text: AI theme should be tracked as a physical-compute and power-infrastructure buildout, not only as GPU, model, or application software exposure.
HBM and advanced-packaging inputs remain a priority chokepoint lane, but Layer 1B must test whether underfollowed suppliers are genuinely mispriced or already discovered.

Data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant is a high-priority small/mid-cap discovery lane because obvious leaders are known while component and service suppliers may be hidden under industrial labels.
Grid, generation, nuclear fuel, and interconnection assets should be mapped as AI capacity constraints with evidence from contracts, load growth, backlog, and regulatory approvals.
Future layers need a current public-company universe screen for market cap, analyst count, liquidity, segment revenue, backlog, customer concentration, and valuation before candidate ranking.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes AI into a physical-compute buildout theme rather than a single software or GPU trade. The strongest first-pass chokepoint lanes are advanced memory/packaging inputs, AI networking/optical interconnect, data-center power/cooling, grid and generation interconnection, semiconductor equipment/materials, and vertical industrial AI software/data workflows. The public-market search should use NVIDIA, TSMC, ASML, Broadcom, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, Constellation, and hyperscalers as reference leaders, but deliberately hunt one to two layers below them for small/mid-cap suppliers with qualification barriers, narrow customer dependencies, low analyst coverage, constrained capacity, or hidden exposure through components, tools, testing, materials, electrical balance-of-plant, nuclear fuel, grid services, and industrial software.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The market has broadly priced HBM producers, but may still misprice narrow suppliers one or two layers beneath them where qualification cycles, materials know-how, inspection/test constraints, or customer concentration create chokepoints.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer $300M-$10B niche suppliers first; allow $10B-$50B only if the supplier has unusually concentrated exposure, near-monopoly share, or low serious analyst coverage relative to quality.
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Start from HBM producers and TSMC/advanced-packaging capacity, then trace suppliers of substrates, bonding materials, thermal materials, inspection tools, probe/test equipment, precision chemicals, and packaging equipment. Prioritize disclosed revenue exposure, named customer wins, capex-linked backlog, and segment margin inflection over broad AI marketing language.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders to validate demand and capex flows: hyperscalers, NVIDIA/AMD/Broadcom, TSMC/ASML, Arista, Vertiv/Eaton, utilities and nuclear/power firms. Lane 2 searches one to two steps below obvious leaders for sub-$10B or sub-$50B public suppliers whose economic exposure is hidden inside materials, tools, packaging inputs, electrical balance-of-plant, cooling components, grid services, testing/inspection, fuel-cycle assets, domain data/software, distributors, and contract manufacturing. Each candidate should be tagged by evidence strength: disclosed customer relationship, filing-backed segment exposure, capex linkage, qualification barrier, backlog/delivery-time evidence, or inferred dependency only.
